question: What is the primary purpose of planning in healthcare management?

options.A: Eliminating all paperwork from the nursing station
options.B: Punishing staff members for poor clinical performance
options.C: Reducing the daily salary budget of the hospital
options.D: Defining goals and strategies for future care

explanation: Planning establishes the roadmap and goals an organization needs to meet future healthcare demands successfully. [learn more](GST321_U1_T5#GST321_U1_T5_h1)

question: A nursing unit that lacks structured planning is most likely to experience what outcome?

options.A: Faster promotion rates for junior nurses
options.B: Reactive operations and compromised patient care
options.C: Instant resolution of chronic staffing shortages
options.D: Higher patient satisfaction and lower costs

explanation: Without planning, units cannot anticipate challenges and instead scramble to react to crises, which harms patient outcomes. [learn more](GST321_U1_T5#GST321_U1_T5_h1)

question: Why must a nursing management plan possess flexibility?

options.A: To reduce the working hours of senior nursing officers
options.B: To make the document longer and more difficult to read
options.C: To ensure the plan never changes under any condition
options.D: To adapt to sudden changes like emergency admissions

explanation: Healthcare environments are unpredictable, requiring plans to adjust smoothly when unexpected clinical emergencies happen. [learn more](GST321_U1_T5#GST321_U1_T5_h2)

question: A feasibility requirement in a healthcare plan means what for the manager?

options.A: Using realistic resources currently available in the system
options.B: Copying plans from foreign hospitals without changes
options.C: Creating goals that require impossible amounts of funding
options.D: Ignoring the basic equipment needs of the ward

explanation: Feasibility ensures that the objectives can actually be met using the personnel and supplies at hand. [learn more](GST321_U1_T5#GST321_U1_T5_h2)

question: Which tier of planning focuses directly on daily shift duties and routines in a ward?
explanation: Operational plans deal with the short-term, day-to-day activities required to run a specific nursing unit smoothly. [learn more](GST321_U1_T5#GST321_U1_T5_h3)

question: A hospital director creating a five-year expansion goal is engaged in what type of planning?
explanation: Strategic plans have a long-term scope and set the overall vision and direction for the entire institution. [learn more](GST321_U1_T5#GST321_U1_T5_h3)

question: What is the very first step in the formal planning process?
explanation: You must first know what you want to achieve before you can evaluate conditions or pick alternatives. [learn more](GST321_U1_T5#GST321_U1_T5_h4)

question: Why is evaluating planning premises important before starting a new project?

options.A: It eliminates the need for any further staff meetings
options.B: It automatically increases the monthly budgetary allocation
options.C: It guarantees that no mistakes will ever happen on the ward
options.D: It helps managers understand current conditions and limitations

explanation: Evaluating premises lets the nurse manager know what resources and constraints exist before drafting solutions. [learn more](GST321_U1_T5#GST321_U1_T5_h4)

question: What tool provides a visual timeline for scheduling tasks and nursing training workshops?
explanation: A Gantt chart is a bar chart that illustrates a project schedule, showing task timelines against calendar dates. [learn more](GST321_U1_T5#GST321_U1_T5_h5)

question: A manager assessing internal ward capabilities alongside external healthcare challenges is using which tool?
explanation: SWOT analysis examines internal strengths and weaknesses alongside external opportunities and threats. [learn more](GST321_U1_T5#GST321_U1_T5_h5)

question: Which factor is a common internal barrier to implementing a new nursing plan?
explanation: Staff members often resist new ways of doing things, which can derail even the best-designed management plans. [learn more](GST321_U1_T5#GST321_U1_T5_h6)

question: Why does poor data collection cause nursing plans to fail?

options.A: It immediately increases the number of patient admissions
options.B: It forces the hospital to buy too many medical supplies
options.C: It causes nurses to work fewer hours on night shifts
options.D: Decisions end up based on guesswork instead of facts

explanation: Accurate data is required to make realistic plans; without it, managers plan based on assumptions. [learn more](GST321_U1_T5#GST321_U1_T5_h6)

question: What action defines the evaluation phase of a management plan?

options.A: Writing the very first draft of the unit budget
options.B: Comparing actual ward performance against initial targets
options.C: Ignoring feedback from patients and junior staff
options.D: Firing nurses who make a single documentation error

explanation: Evaluation measures what was actually achieved against what was planned to see if goals were met. [learn more](GST321_U1_T5#GST321_U1_T5_h7)

question: What should a nurse manager do when evaluation reveals that medication errors have increased?

options.A: Wait several years before taking any action
options.C: Hide the error records from the medical director
options.D: Stop all clinical audits across the hospital

explanation: Evaluation is meant to trigger corrective action when performance falls short of safety or operational standards. [learn more](GST321_U1_T5#GST321_U1_T5_h7)
